summary: The §6A settle/signal/dry-run repairs look coherent against the machine-checked table, but resuming a pre-epoch ledger can newly infra-gate a still-retryable record that the old planner would have run. The suite’s signature independence test also asserts less than it claims, so the next axis swap could land green.

findings.title: Pre-§6A lifetime attempts_infra is loaded as the streak and re-gates records old decide would RUN
findings.evidence:
if "attempts_infra_total" not in raw:
    # ... do NOT seed the streak from anything: the
    # gate value is whatever that older ledger recorded, unchanged, so upgrading
    # the runner cannot silently un-gate (or re-gate) a route.
    st.attempts_infra_total = st.attempts_infra
findings.why_wrong: Before §6A, attempts_infra was a lifetime counter and decide() consulted infra only on the no-record branch, so a route could hold a final RETRY_RECORD with record budget left and attempts_infra already at infra_budget and still be planned RUN. Epoch 2 both (a) treats that same field as a consecutive streak and (b) applies the infra gate on the final-record branch. Loading an old ledger therefore preserves the lifetime tally as the streak and SKIP_EXHAUSTED-unsettles a route the previous runner would have retried — false gap / exit 1. Concrete tuple: (epoch-1 ledger, attempts_infra=infra_budget, RETRY_RECORD on disk, record spent < record_budget, skip_terminal) → new decide SKIP_EXHAUSTED settled=False; old decide RUN. The accounting-epoch warning only narrates the killed-vs-record split, not this infra lifetime→streak re-gate, and TestAccountingEpochIsAnnounced/_aged_ledger never builds attempts_infra at budget with record budget left. --retry-infra-exhausted recovers, but only if the operator realises the gate is a migration artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: On epoch-1→2 load, either clear attempts_infra when a final non-fabricable-or-any final record is already on disk (lifetime≠streak), or auto-offer the infra recovery for epoch upgrades and make the warning name this case. Add a regression: aged ledger with attempts_infra=infra_budget + RETRY_RECORD + record budget left must plan RUN (or clear loudly), not unsettled SKIP_EXHAUSTED.

findings.title: TestPatternIndependence asserts only attempts_killed==0, not counter equality across stderr
findings.evidence:
Once ``signalled`` decides the class, a fault pattern in the (shared) stream must not be
able to move a single counter after the process has exited.
...
self.assertEqual(
    state.get(task.key).attempts_killed, 0,
    "a non-signalled exit charged the ambiguity axis because of text in "
    "a stream the CARLA server shares")
findings.why_wrong: The docstring claims post-exit stderr cannot move any counter, and that this would have caught round three’s pattern-widening budget swap. The body only checks attempts_killed == 0 per (status, rc, stderr) cell. It never snapshots the full budgets() vector and never asserts equality across stderr_text for fixed (status, rc). A regression that demotes/abnormal-classifies into infra or that fails to charge record/tickruntime still passes while killed stays 0 — the same “test never went red for the claim” shape that previously let axis bugs through.
findings.suggested_fix: For each (status, rc), compute expected budgets once from signalled-only classification, then assert state.get(task.key).budgets() equals that expectation for every stderr_text; optionally also assert outcome class is identical across stderr for non-signalled rcs.

findings.title: Normative 6A.5 table driver does not check requeue on sets_finished: no rows
findings.evidence:
elif finished == "no":
    self.assertFalse(st.finished, f"{klass} x {on_disk}: the table says this never "
                                  f"settles on its own")
else:
    self.assertEqual(finished, "when_spent")
    ...
    self.assertTrue(requeue, ...)
findings.why_wrong: when_spent rows assert both settlement and requeue while budget remains. finished=no rows (all NEVER_STARTED cells, NO_FINAL_RECORD infra charges, TORN_DOWN non-ACCEPT, FATAL) only assert finished is false after the first settle. A bug that returns requeue=False on the first infra charge under infra_budget=2 — or requeue=True on TORN_DOWN — leaves the machine-checked table green. Within-run retry count and drain behaviour are part of the termination argument the table is supposed to pin.
findings.suggested_fix: For finished=no: if budget_charged is infra and attempts_infra < infra_budget, assert requeue is True; if budget_charged is none (or FATAL/NEVER_STARTED at exhaustion), assert requeue is False.
